discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed. The matcher now accepts `false`, `False`, and `FALSE`, the three spellings both js-yaml's JSON schema and the SDK's yaml parser read as boolean false (`no`/`off` stay strings in both, so they are correctly left alone). Test added.

This used to resolve local-CLI status from the provider registry; it now requires matching `providerAuth`. When those facts are absent or don't match the selected provider it silently becomes "not a local-CLI provider" — a `claude-code` user gets "Check your model connection in Settings → API Providers" rather than "Sign in again with the `claude` CLI". `resolveCredentialFailureAction` at line 291 has the same gate and returns an "Open API providers" action instead of `null`.

The live paths try to keep these facts synchronized, so the happy path is covered — it's the fallback that changed. Preserving built-in auth behaviour when catalog facts aren't available, or making "unknown auth" an explicit state rather than a silent negative, would keep this correct without reaching back into `@cline/llms`.

Half right, and the fix is the other half. The `null` is deliberate: an explicit `undefined` is swallowed by the parameter default, so the unlisted-model case would silently get the effort options instead of none. The bug was that my edit to widen the signature to `| null` did not apply, leaving the annotation saying `| undefined` while the body already normalised `null`. Signature corrected rather than the call site.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Added in 3fe2f2a: `sqlite-cron-store.bun-test.ts` runs under `bun test` (the Desktop runtime, bun:sqlite) and (1) asserts bun:sqlite binds named parameters by exact token — unprefixed keys bind NULL, prefixed keys bind the value; (2) end-to-end: claimDueRuns claims a due one-off run (status=running).
